block.title: Store capsule: title-safe vertical crop, fighter screaming past burning hull
block.positive: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering, bold dark outlines, saturated limited palette, near-square arcade poster composition, subtle CRT scanline glow; store capsule artwork built to stay readable at small size, ultra-detailed with clean vector shapes. Centered and enormous, filling the right two-thirds of a square frame: the forward third of a mechanical sea-creature battleship's head — a flared iron jaw lined with dark turret barnacles, one great round sensor eye glowing hot violet at the top third of the image, armor plates stepping back into deep rust-shadow. Slicing diagonally across the lower-left foreground, nose toward the upper-right corner of the frame and enormous in perspective, the polished steel-blue nose-cone and swept wingroot of a fighter — cyan canopy edge catching the boss's eye-light, a single orange engine flare blown long behind it off-frame — the two machines on an unavoidable collision course frozen one frame before it. Between them, sparse pink bright-core bullets float like angry fireflies, few enough to read individually even at capsule size. Above the jaw-line, across the very top of the frame, straight-on blocky arcade capitals hold the game's name in a warm vertical gradient from pale yellow through orange into red, thick dark navy outlines, white top-highlight, generous drop shadow: the words "SHMUP CUP". Background a clean lifted deep-navy starfield with the faintest violet nebula breath, everything else kept empty so the title, the eye, and the nose-cone do all the selling. Never pure black. The text in the image must read exactly "SHMUP CUP" and nothing else.
